extracted.intended_audience: members of Parliament, policymakers, and the informed public concerned with East India Company governance and colonial fiscal policy
extracted.subtask_description: A late-18th-century parliamentary speech critiquing the East India Company's handling of consolidated debts in the Carnatic (Arcot), arguing for inquiry, fairness, and protection of native and honest creditors while exposing corruption and maladministration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require inquiry before paying claimed debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment ordered "without any sort of inquiry into its authenticity,--without a single step taken to settle even the amount of the demand,--without an attempt so much as to ascertain the real persons claiming a sum..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ministry should not authorize payment of large consolidated claims without taking steps to verify authenticity, settle the amount due, and ascertain the real persons claiming. Surrounding explanation emphasizes that paying on mere assertions invites fraud and makes detection impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put burden of proof on claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: Ought not ministry to have said to the creditors, '...prove that you have acted by lawful authority; prove, at least, that your money has been bonâ fide advanced; entitle yourself to my protection by the fairness and fulness of the communications you make'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request full documentary proof and lawful authority from those demanding public payment. The speaker argues it is reasonable and honest to require creditors to prove their claims before granting public protection or payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not indiscriminately establish mixed valid and fraudulent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: In a case where many valid and many fraudulent claims are blended together, [it is wrong] 'to establish them all' indiscriminately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where claims are a mixture of valid and fraudulent, the correct policy is discrimination and investigation, not blanket establishment. The ministry's approach of recognizing all claims is condemned as facilitating fraud and injustice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertain proprietors and require lists of claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: No attempt so much as to ascertain the real persons claiming a sum which rises in the accounts ...--without an attempt made to ascertain the proprietors, of whom no list has ever yet been laid before the Court of Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before payment, compile and present lists identifying proprietors/claimants. The absence of such lists leaves room for collusive shuffles and prevents accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid paying consolidated debts that do not state the consolidated amount
rubrics_metrics.description: The Consolidation of 1777 ... is probably the first debt ever assuming the title of Consolidation that did not express what the amount of the sum consolidated was.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consolidation should explicitly state the amounts consolidated. Consolidating unspecified or fluctuating sums invites manipulation and obscures accountability; ministers should refuse such opaque consolidations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and prioritize bona fide native creditors
rubrics_metrics.description: The creditors most certainly not fraudulent are the natives ... by exhausting the whole revenues of the Carnatic, nothing is left for them. They lent bonâ fide ... They ought with every generous mind to claim their first charities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When distributing limited public revenues, give priority to native creditors who lent bona fide and are impoverished, rather than to influential or collusive European creditors. The speaker frames this as both a moral duty and a matter of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent conflicts of interest in adjudicating claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The members of [the Mayor's] court were themselves creditors, and therefore could not sit as judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial or quasi-judicial bodies deciding creditor claims should not contain members who are themselves creditors or otherwise have direct stakes; avoiding conflicts of interest is essential for fair adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely solely on claimants or others to detect fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: He trusts ... that the best warranted claimants will exert themselves in bringing to light those debts which will not bear an inquiry. What he will not do himself he is persuaded, (I suppose,) as there may not be a fund sufficient for every description of creditors, that the best warranted claimants will exert themselves ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The government must take active measures to detect fraud rather than expecting honest creditors or third parties to expose fraudulent claims. Relying on others to do the detection is criticized as naive and ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow prescribed legal procedures and powers for investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The ministers have not been satisfied with authorizing the payment of this demand without such inquiry as the act has prescribed; but they have added ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministers should comply with statutory or prescribed procedures for inquiry and investigation before authorizing payments. Ignoring prescribed legal safeguards undermines legitimacy and enables malfeasance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid granting retroactive or excessive interest to inflate claims
rubrics_metrics.description: They have added the arrear of twelve per cent interest, from the year 1777 to the year 1784, to make a new capital ... and has again grafted on this meliorated stock a perpetual annuity of six per cent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers should scrutinize the application of interest and avoid compounding or granting excessive retroactive interest that serves to dramatically inflate public liability. The speech presents such additions as a form of 'consolidated corruption.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not confer only with agents of alleged creditors
rubrics_metrics.description: He fairly tells you that through the course of the whole business he has never conferred with any but the agents of the pretended creditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers must engage with a broad set of parties and not consult exclusively with agents representing one side (especially the claimants), since that fosters collusion and biased outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government recovery/reconstruction policy: support population via expenditure not extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: In order that the people, after a long period of vexation and plunder, may be in a condition to maintain government, government must begin by maintaining them. Here the road to economy lies not through receipt, but through expense;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-conflict or post-plunder economic recovery requires public expenditure to restore population, agriculture, irrigation (reservoirs), and productive capacity, rather than immediate revenue extraction. The speech uses the Carnatic's lack of water/irrigation infrastructure to argue for investment-first policy.
